version.changelog: Worker app now on Google Play as well as the App Store; adds a free first-mission trial link for businesses without an account.

llm.summary: This skill coherently connects an agent to the Errand service to quote and dispatch paid physical errands, with clear user confirmation and consent requirements.

dimensions.detail: Use of an API key and network requests to errand.be is proportionate for a paid service integration, and optional source reporting is disclosed as consent-based with instructions to leave it unset otherwise.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a Markdown-only skill requiring curl and an ERRANDAI_API_KEY; it also documents optional remote MCP setup, but does not ship executable scripts, hidden installers, package dependencies, or automatic setup steps.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly requires coverage and quote checks before dispatch, requires the user's explicit yes to a stated total price before moving money, and limits cancellation/status/result actions to Errand dispatch workflows.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No local persistence, privilege escalation, background service, or memory-writing behavior is present; the only persistent setup discussed is user-controlled environment configuration or optional MCP registration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The external API calls, location data, worker instructions, photo evidence, quotes, dispatches, status polling, cancellation, and result fetching all match the stated purpose of sending a real worker to a physical location.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, understand that this skill can spend prepaid Errand balance and send location-specific instructions to a real worker. Keep the API key private, only opt into source reporting if you want that analytics attribution, review the quoted total before approving dispatch, and remember that cancellation is only available before a worker accepts.
llm.findings:
[E1] expected: The flagged external transmission is an authenticated capabilities request to the service the skill is designed to use; the artifact discloses the destination, API key requirement, and request headers.
[SQP-3] expected: The Korean-field requirement is purpose-aligned because the dispatched worker reads those fields on a phone in Seoul; it constrains task payload language, not the user's general interaction language.
[AIG] expected: A.I.G reported no SARIF results, and the inspected artifact does not show instruction hijacking, memory poisoning, remote code execution, embedded malicious code, persistence, tool spoofing, or unsafe dependencies.
